title: Forecourt: the station hall, the lane gardens and the service yard
caption: The critic's three forecourt points from re-score 2: the station hall seen cut open read empty, the lane gardens were parallel strips, and a service path north of the court ended at a hedge. Before on the left of each pair, after on the right; the plan from above at the end.

sections.title: Out of the station
sections.caption: The security room now has a pair of ticket machines with the lit fare map over them by the exit, a yellow guide line from the entrance through the gate to the exit, a yellow exit arrow on the floor past the gate, and ceiling light on the floor. The dark mat inside the doorway is gone: a steel sill and the daylight through the exit instead. The room itself is laid out as before; the gate scene has the same fittings and a yellow 出口 EXIT sign over the exit.

sections.title: The same room in the gate scene
sections.caption: The exit sign over the door, the ticket machines between the notice screen and the exit, the guide line and the floor arrow.

sections.title: The lane gardens
sections.caption: The strips are gone. The avenue's bed is planted in layers and its back edge steps in and out, and the gardens either side are drifts of different depths with a big cherry and a black pine standing free, maples and a ginkgo, rocks in threes and a hedge that steps in and out. A gap in the lane's hedge leads on stepping stones to a gravel court with a bench and a stone lantern; Eric can walk there.

sections.title: From above
sections.caption: The service path is now a service yard: a closed gate with a STAFF ONLY sign on the court's edge, roll cages and a delivery bike inside, and a roofed refuse store across its far end instead of the hedge. The gardens along the lane read as gardens from above too.
